In summary, our research is concerned with
the specific functions of the different isoforms of JNK in the brain.
the specific functions of JNKs in the central nervous system and the role of the different isoforms in neuronal survival.
the pathophysiological functions and the therapeutic potential of JNK isoform specific inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
JNK1, JNK2 and JNK3 are not redundant in the brain, but have specific and distinct pathophysiological functions.
the specific deletion of JNK isoform(s) does not necessarily lead to a decrease of phosphorylated c-Jun.
JNK1 and JNK2 are involved in cell death pathways in the brain and JNK3 is involved in the regulation of axonal degeneration and seizure activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specific deletion of JNK isoform(s) is beneficial to the brain in the case of axonal injury and neurotoxicity.
JNK1 is the main JNK isoform expressed and activated in the brain and that JNK1 and JNK3 are both involved in the survival and death of neurons in the brain.

JNK3 is the major JNK isoform in the brain and that JNK1 and JNK3 are the major JNKs that mediate cell death in response to ischemia and excitotoxicity, whereas JNK3 is involved in neurodegeneration following axon injury and JNK3 and JNK2 are involved in the degeneration of dopaminergic SNC neurons following neurotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
JNK1 and JNK3 isoforms are involved in the pathogenesis of ischemia and excitotoxicity.
the JNK isoforms have specific functions in the brain.
JNK1, JNK2 and JNK3 have different functions in the brain and their deletion has distinct consequences on the survival of neurons in different brain areas.
